Browse Hungarian KRESZ traffic signs by category. Open a category to see every sign in that group, then tap a sign for a full-size image and description. Descriptions follow the device language: Hungarian when the locale is Hungarian, English otherwise.

Replacement sign diagrams are based on Hungarian KRESZ tables and Wikimedia Commons SVG road-sign diagrams. Police-signal, lane-use light and some road-marking drawings are original educational diagrams. Original raster artwork is kept where no matching diagram was available.
Left turn in front of the officer
If you come from the side (green arrows), you may go. If you face the chest or back (red stop marks), you must halt. Officer signals override signs and lights.
Like an amber light: stop if you can; leave the junction if you are already in it. Pedestrians must not step onto the carriageway.
Traffic from the officer\'s right (green arrows) may go ahead, turn right, or turn left behind the officer on the curved path. Every other approach must stop.
Traffic from the officer\'s left (green arrows) may go ahead, turn right, or turn left in front of the officer on the curved path. Every other approach must stop.
Arms hang at the sides — same rule as both arms out. Sides (green arrows): go. Chest or back (red stop marks): halt.
The officer beckons toward the body (yellow arrows pointing in). Speed up only if you are already allowed to go.
The officer pumps an arm up and down (yellow arrows). Slow down only if you are already allowed to go.

Stop for the white-rimmed red disc or a raised arm. A public-space warden and other entitled persons (military traffic regulator, disaster management, customs, fire, transport authority inspector) may give the same signal. Officer signals override signs and lights.
Stop when a moving police vehicle signals with lights, a disc or lamp waved up and down, a loudspeaker, or a STOP marking. Follow the instruction. Officer signals override signs and lights.
Stop for a flagman or civil-guard flagman showing a red disc or a red lamp, often on a stand. Advance warning is the railway or roadworks warning sign with the signalman plate.
